title: Joint-Function Coverage in White-Box Prediction Security
summary: The current prediction-security notion gives a single-function guarantee; whether several closure functions jointly enable an attack and require a stronger definition remains open.

formal_statement.body: For the prediction-security model of a white-box circuit, in which a pair $(C,E)$ is $d$-th-order prediction-secure when every adversary has negligible prediction advantage, determine whether the joint behavior of multiple functions in the $d$-th-order closure can enable an attack that is not covered by the existing single-function guarantee. In a first-order Boolean-masked white-box AES implementation, two circuit nodes may compute masks $f_1$ and $f_2$ of a first-round S-box output bit, and an adversary may form $\tilde{f}=f_1\oplus f_2$ in $F^{(1)}(C)$; establish whether this jointly constructed function can produce such an attack and, if so, strengthen the prediction-security definition so that it covers joint-function attacks.

scope.domain: Prediction security for white-box circuits, including first-order Boolean-masked white-box AES.
assumptions: In the motivating example, two circuit nodes compute masks f₁ and f₂ of a first-round S-box output bit.
parameters: d: the order defining prediction security and the corresponding function closure
(C,E): the pair evaluated by the prediction-security model
f₁, f₂, and f̃: two node-computed masks and their XOR combination in the first-order closure
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether multiple functions in the d-th-order closure, including the first-order XOR construction, can jointly enable an attack outside the single-function guarantee and, if so, strengthen prediction security to cover it.

citations.label: Attacks and Countermeasures for White-box Designs

progress.summary: The source gives the negligible-advantage definition and then flags joint behavior by multiple functions as a possible attack avenue. Its masked-AES example leaves both the attack question and any corresponding strengthening unresolved.
citation_labels: Alex Biryukov et al., Attacks and Countermeasures for White-box Designs
